The team was discussing the changes in the semantic specification and construction formalisms. The team also discussed the pros and cons of different notations.

The team agreed that the constructions they were working on were not very specific. They were also not very grammatically precise. They thought that they should separate the problem out and focus on the most important things.

The semantic specification is a set of constraints that define the meaning of the utterances in the discourse. The constraints are divided into two categories: attribute-value and semantic constraints. The former are value fillings, and the latter are bindings. The binding constraints are semantic effects, which are not too restrictive. The semantic effects are not used to match, but to constrain the possible values of the variables. The discourse- level effects are used to constrict the possible meanings of the discourse units.

The team would be building a space, which would be a mental construction. The construction would be based on the context of the discourse. The team would have to figure out how to identify the referents and how to handle the different aspects of the construction.
The domains in mental spaces are time, space, discourse, Bayes, sarcasm, and irony.
